policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV explicitly reads 'Greater joy,' distinguishing χαράν from χάριν; the note is only an alternative rendering and does not alter that judgment.
ASV's 'walking in the truth' expresses the definite article τῇ; the alternative-rendering note concerns another phrase.
ASV's 'and strangers withal' reflects the emphatic καὶ τοῦτο ξένους construction, distinguishing τοῦτο from a repeated εἰς τοὺς.
ASV's 'the Gentiles' can render either ἐθνικῶν or ἐθνῶν, and no mapped textual note distinguishes them; retain the base fallback.
ASV's 'welcome such' does not distinguish ὑπολαμβάνειν from ἀπολαμβάνειν; the note is only an alternative rendering, so retain the base fallback.
ASV's explicit 'somewhat' renders τι and distinguishes it from omission.
ASV's singular 'thou knowest' distinguishes singular οἶδας from plural οἴδατε.
ASV explicitly says 'to write unto thee,' including the singular recipient represented by σοι and distinguishing γράψαι σοι from γράφειν.
ASV's infinitive 'to write' does not distinguish present γράφειν from aorist γράψαι, and no textual note decides it; retain the base fallback.
ASV's 'to see thee' does not expose whether the Greek pronoun precedes or follows the infinitive; retain the base fallback.
